A_general.open_code_note: No official public source repository or package was found in the prepared evidence. Greenhouse documents a hosted MCP server layered over the Harvest v3 API; the endpoint implementation is not public.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.us.greenhouse.io/mcp — official US-hosted endpoint documented for Claude Code and ChatGPT setup; the Greenhouse security FAQ says US hosting is current. Its public metadata advertises the same resource name and scope as the input endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MCP-specific price is not published in the reviewed materials. Greenhouse says access depends on subscription tier and admin configuration, and advises contacting the account team about access and pricing.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Greenhouse Recruiting pricing page does not publish amounts in the captured page; pricing is provided through sales contact.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP is available on Core, Plus, and Pro tiers, subject to open-beta access and organization configuration. No per-call MCP charge or MCP-specific quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Site Admin setup and scope configuration are required. Users need an eligible tier, an individual Greenhouse account, enabled organization scopes, and their own product permissions. AI clients require OAuth 2.0 PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration; redirect URLs must be approved. No native MCP IP allowlist, geo restriction, or device-based control is provided.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls eligible tiers and OAuth service; organization Site Admin controls MCP scopes and redirect URL patterns; end users consent to permitted scopes and retain their Greenhouse role permissions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official documentation describes the server as exposing a subset of Harvest v3 API capabilities as tools, including candidate, application, job, interview, scorecard, and organization data/actions. It does not publish an official tool-by-tool list. The Claude connector directory lists 159 exact tool names; these are recorded as third-party additions in actions.json.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The security FAQ describes confirmation-required operations as returning a plain-language summary and stopping until the client sends confirmation. General result and error schemas are not published in the reviewed sources.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No official documentation found describing MCP resources.
No official documentation found describing MCP prompts.

Greenhouse states it supports auditability through Greenhouse-managed logging for supported MCP activity. The security FAQ does not specify logged fields, retention period, or customer-visible MCP event details.

Protected-resource metadata at the origin and endpoint-path URLs reports resource https://mcp.greenhouse.io and https://mcp.greenhouse.io/mcp respectively; both identify Greenhouse MCP Server, authorization server https://auth.greenhouse.io, scope greenhouse:mcp_client, and bearer token in header. Authorization-server metadata lists authorization_code and refresh_token grants, code response type, S256 PKCE, Dynamic Client Registration at https://auth.greenhouse.io/register, and token endpoint auth methods none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and private_key_jwt. Greenhouse docs specify short-lived access tokens (one hour), refresh tokens valid until 14 consecutive days of inactivity, and revocation endpoint https://auth.greenhouse.io/revoke. OpenID scopes_supported are openid, profile, email; these are distinct from the resource scope greenhouse:mcp_client.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth bearer access token is sent in the Authorization header. The endpoint's supplied POST probe returned HTTP 415 unsupported_media_type with the message “Content-Type must be application/json.” No WWW-Authenticate value was provided in the supplied evidence.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE (S256), Dynamic Client Registration, authorization_code and refresh_token grants; resource scopes_supported: ["greenhouse:mcp_client"]; authorization-server scopes_supported: ["openid","profile","email"]; token endpoint auth methods: ["none","client_secret_basic","client_secret_post","private_key_jwt"]; revocation_endpoint: https://auth.greenhouse.io/revoke. Access tokens expire after one hour; refresh tokens remain valid until 14 consecutive days of inactivity, per official security FAQ.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No MCP Elicitation capability is documented. The server does require a human-confirmation round trip for five high-stakes actions, but the documentation does not identify MCP Elicitation as the mechanism.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: For five specified actions, the server returns a plain-language summary and stops; the AI client can present it and send confirmation before execution.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Site Admins configure available Harvest API categories and read/write scopes in Dev Center > MCP Access, and can manage approved redirect URL patterns. If no scopes are configured, the documented default is seven read-only scopes: applications, candidates, job interview stages, jobs, rejection reasons, scorecards, and users. Saving an empty selection removes access to all Greenhouse data. Users must reconnect after scope changes.
No general MCP error format or reporting facility found. The endpoint's supplied unauthenticated POST evidence reports an HTTP 415 JSON error object.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Observed endpoint probe error shape: {"error":"unsupported_media_type","message":"Content-Type must be application/json."}

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The server exposes authenticated Harvest v3 API operations through a hosted MCP endpoint. The server's initialize instructions were not publicly available in the evidence. Official guidance is provided outside the server through Greenhouse support articles, while the MCP interface itself is OAuth protected.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs describe read and write scopes, but no MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were published. Every DELETE endpoint is blocked. The Claude directory lists 159 actions, including writes, but tool schemas/annotations are not published there. 2. The server enforces confirmation for five high-stakes actions: rejecting an applicant, merging candidates, hiring an applicant, creating or updating an offer, and bulk-revoking user permissions. It returns a summary and stops pending client confirmation. 3. Organization scopes are an admin-configured ceiling; individual OAuth consent can select among available categories; Greenhouse user roles/permissions further restrict access. Admin scope changes invalidate all active MCP tokens; account deactivation invalidates that user's tokens. Redirect URL allowlisting is checked on authorization. 4. Admins can configure read-only by enabling only read scopes. No MCP-specific department/division partitioning, IP allowlisting, geo restriction, or device control; existing product permissions can scope user data. Docs describe sandbox use by signing out before authorizing, and a US hosted endpoint in setup instructions. 5. Attachments expose metadata and a download link; the MCP server does not fetch or return actual file content. No direct MCP control for department-level data partitioning. 6. No MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, date-range caps, or per-call costs found. 7. Public code unavailable; parameter validation, coercion, alias correction, and operator overrides are unknown. 8. Greenhouse claims managed logging/auditability for supported MCP activity; details and retention are not stated. 9. No feedback/rating/survey/report tool was identified in the 159-name catalogue list. No vendor upsell tool/message documented. 10. No server-delivered skills or behavioral initialize text found. Official user guidance recommends setup and safe practices; catalogue descriptions are absent. 11. Server says it does not store or persist data. No evidence that past agent behavior changes subsequent outputs or available tools. 12. Input endpoint is a hosted Greenhouse MCP server over Harvest v3. A second official US endpoint is documented; no sub-server hierarchy is documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, run-script, or similar escape-hatch tool identified in the listed tools.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: “To make MCP read-only, enable only the read scopes.”
“For those five actions, the MCP server returns a plain-language summary of what is about to happen and stops.”
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Greenhouse documents distinct global and US-hosted MCP endpoints. Its tool availability is dynamically controlled by admin-configured OAuth scopes; tools corresponding to disabled scopes do not appear for users.

E_aggregated.action_count: 159 third-party listed names; official tool-name count not published
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official tool-by-tool list was found; Greenhouse's official security FAQ says it does not expose a separate public MCP tool-by-tool changelog and describes a subset of Harvest v3 API. The Claude connector directory is a third-party listing and states “Show all 159 tools”; all 159 listed names are in actions.json as catalogue additions, with enabled_by_default unknown. No names are published by the official sources. APIs.io and mcpyet list the server but provide no action names. Work Insiders explicitly says Greenhouse shares its tool list only after sign-in and gives capabilities from official docs rather than exact names. The 159 directory names are not verified as the exact current tools of this endpoint; availability varies with enabled scopes and user permissions.
E_aggregated.token_method: No public implementation or verbatim tools/list and initialize output was available; third-party names without schemas cannot support a context token estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP exposes only a subset of the Harvest v3 API; Greenhouse states that not all API endpoints may be exposed. The reviewed material does not enumerate the omitted endpoints or map all Greenhouse UI operations to MCP availability. The MCP server permanently blocks DELETE endpoints, so delete operations available through other product surfaces cannot be performed through MCP. [Official security FAQ]

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Greenhouse recommends data-quality practices for stronger analysis, including consistent interview stage names and completed scorecards/interview kits. The documentation does not describe these recommendations as server-enforced. It also advises users to configure AI tools, DLP, and retention controls; client-side controls remain customer responsibilities.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Greenhouse states MCP access is scoped to admin-enabled categories and existing user permissions; credentials go only to Greenhouse, while the AI tool holds an OAuth token. The server says it does not store or persist customer data and does not return attachment file contents. It says access tokens are checked against an encrypted database reference on every request and that revocation applies on the next call. Every DELETE endpoint is blocked, with five high-stakes actions requiring explicit confirmation.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes Greenhouse MCP as a governed way to connect approved AI tools to live recruiting data, with admin-managed controls and support for auditability through Greenhouse-managed logging for supported activity.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented authorization and DELETE/confirmation controls are described as server-enforced. Audit logging is promised but implementation details and retention are not documented. Data non-persistence and attachment-content limits are stated in the security FAQ. Advice about client configuration, data loss prevention, retention, and user training is guidance, not a server control.

contradictions: The Claude connector directory describes broad write capability and lists 159 tools, while Greenhouse publishes no official tool-by-tool list and says tool availability is constrained by organization scopes and user permissions. These catalogue names and claims cannot be confirmed as universally enabled on the input endpoint.

Official setup docs describe seven default read-only scopes when MCP Access is not configured; once an admin saves scope selections, those selections replace the defaults, and saving with none selected removes data access. The tool set is therefore configuration-dependent, whereas the third-party directory gives a static total of 159.

The input endpoint's supplied probe returned HTTP 415 for a request missing the required JSON Content-Type, while the prepared endpoint check reports HTTP 401 for an OAuth-protected MCP endpoint. These are different request conditions and are not evidence of a server behavior conflict.
observations_for_research: Scope configuration changes which corresponding tools are exposed; users must reconnect after admin scope changes.
Access combines organization-wide scope ceiling, per-tool user consent, and existing Greenhouse role permissions.
The server imposes a blanket DELETE block and requires confirmation for a documented subset of high-stakes writes.
Authorization is per-user OAuth with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration; the security FAQ says redirect allowlisting is checked at each authorization.
The server reports no MCP-side persistence, while client retention/caching follows the AI provider's policies.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ official article copies and rendered scripts, endpoint pages, pricing/legal pages, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt. No official repository or package was listed. The Claude directory is a third-party catalogue; its exact names are included only as catalogue additions, not asserted as the official tool list. Other catalogues did not add a reliable exact name list. The endpoint origin and path-specific OAuth metadata were supplied as pre-fetched evidence; no OAuth login or mutation was performed.
